title: UHF RFID Inlay — Roll-to-Roll Tag Component
summary: UHF RFID inlays are the chip-on-antenna passive component supplied on PET film at 2,000-20,000 inlays per roll for label converters and tag makers. They ship wet (PSA + release liner) for label lamination or dry (no adhesive) for rigid-housing embedding, on dogbone, near-field, square and web-44 antennas. Every roll is 100% RF-tested and ships with a per-lot sensitivity histogram, yield report and GS1 SGTIN-96 EPC manifest for Walmart T2/T3, Target, Macy's and Auburn ARC programmes.

sections.title: What a UHF inlay actually is
sections.intro: Strip away the face stock, the print and the die-cut and what actually answers the reader is deceptively small: a UHF chip flip-mounted onto a metal strap, bonded to an etched-aluminium dipole antenna on a 50 µm PET web. That is the inlay — a sub-component, not a finished label — resonating across the global UHF RAIN band of 860-960 MHz that each region then carves into its own narrower window. The silicon barely changes between programmes; the antenna is the part you actually specify, and it ships in six standard geometries.
bullets: Dogbone 96 × 22 mm — apparel hang tag + shipping label workhorse.
Rectangular 70 × 18 mm — carton labels and mid-size tags.
Short dipole 50 × 12 mm — product labels + compact tags.
Near-field 27 × 10 mm — pharma vial + jewelry + cosmetic.
Square 50 × 50 mm — on-metal with spacer + general purpose.
Web 44 × 44 mm — retail price label + library shelf.

image.alt: Annotated anatomy of a UHF RFID inlay: a UHF chip on a metal strap at the centre of an etched-aluminium dogbone dipole antenna, all carried on a 50 µm PET web, tuned across the 860-960 MHz UHF band.

sections.title: Wet, dry, converted: one chip, three finish states
sections.intro: The same chip and antenna leave the line in one of three finish states, and which one you order is dictated entirely by the process waiting downstream. A dry inlay is the bare core; a wet inlay adds the pressure-sensitive adhesive and release liner a label converter laminates from; a converted inlay is that inlay already built into printed face stock — at which point it has stopped being a component and become a finished label.
bullets: Wet inlay — PSA layer + silicone-coated PET release liner; for converters laminating into thermal-transfer / direct-thermal / synthetic label stock.
Dry inlay — no adhesive, no liner; for embedding into ID-1 / CR-80 PVC card body, hard ABS / polycarbonate housings, over-molded silicone wristbands, RTI tags.
Same chip + antenna available in either format — choice is downstream-process driven.

image.alt: Three finish states of one UHF inlay, left to right: a dry inlay with no adhesive or liner, a wet inlay adding a PSA adhesive layer and a silicone-coated PET release liner, and a converted inlay laminated into printed face stock to become a finished label.

dataHighlight.heading: {chip:nxp-ucode-9:name} read sensitivity — best-in-class for dense-reader tunnel + freezer + 12-18 m read range
dataHighlight.text: Chip sensitivity dictates how far and how reliably an inlay reads. {chip:impinj-m770:name} (-22.7 dBm) + {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} (-22.1 dBm) + {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} (-22.7 dBm) form the Impinj M700 family with Autopilot tuning and 96-bit EPC + variable user memory; {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} is the fastest encoder for high-speed print-and-apply, {chip:impinj-m770:short_name} + {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} favoured for retail item-level + carton. {chip:nxp-ucode-9:name} (-23.5 dBm best-in-class, 96-bit EPC + 0-bit user; {chip:nxp-ucode-9xe:short_name} variant 128-bit EPC; UCODE 9xm variant configurable up to 496-bit EPC + 752-bit user) is best-in-class for dense-reader tunnel + freezer + 12-18 m read range applications; {chip:nxp-ucode-8:short_name} / 8m (-21.0 dBm) is the established platform for general retail. {chip:impinj-monza-r6:name} / R6-P (-20.5 dBm, 96-bit EPC, 32 bit user) is the proven workhorse with 5+ years of Auburn ARC audit history. Antenna geometry pairs with the chip — dogbone 96 mm for apparel hang tag + shipping label, rectangular 70 mm for carton, short dipole 50 mm for product label, near-field 27 mm for pharma vial + jewelry, square 50 mm for on-metal with spacer, web 44 mm for retail price + library. Region tuning is at antenna geometry — Region 1 (EU 865-868 MHz), Region 2 (Americas 902-928 MHz), Region 3 (Asia-Pacific 920-926 MHz), or universal.

sections.title: The reference facts, at a glance
sections.intro: Everything a converter or programme reviewer cross-checks against the datasheet — roll format, frequency and regulatory caps, tag QA, reader compatibility, EPC pre-encoding, retailer readiness, procurement and the not-this list — gathered into one scannable block.

features.title: Roll format & converter compatibility
features.text: Standard rolls — 2,000 / 5,000 / 10,000 / 20,000 inlays on 3″ (76.2 mm) core. Web width — 50 / 85 / 110 mm (matches Mark Andy P5/P7, Nilpeter FA-17, MPS EF-Symjet, Edale FL3). Pitch — 14, 18, 22, 25, 30, 35 mm or custom centre-to-centre on the web. Pitch tolerance ±0.5 mm; chip position ±0.3 mm — the spec converting lines need to hold first-pass encoding at 99%+.

features.title: Frequency & regulatory framework
features.text: FCC Part 15.247 — 902-928 MHz unlicensed (US, Canada, Mexico, parts of LATAM); 4 W EIRP cap. ETSI EN 302 208 — 865-868 MHz (EU + UK + Norway + Switzerland); 2 W ERP cap. MIC Japan — 916.7-923.5 MHz; 1 W EIRP. ACMA Australia — 920-926 MHz; 4 W EIRP cap. Each chip is regional-tuned — antenna designs available for Region 1 (EU), Region 2 (Americas), Region 3 (Asia-Pacific) or universal.

features.title: Tag QA — Auburn ARC + GS1 EPCIS
features.text: Auburn University RFID Lab ARC categories — Q (high-volume retail), W (apparel), X (cold-DC), G (general purpose), L (logistics), M (RTI / metal-near). ARC-spec assessment runs each antenna design through 60-cm + 6-m anechoic chamber tests with population sweep. GS1 EPCIS 2.0 (ISO/IEC 19987:2021) downstream event capture — Commission, ObjectEvent, AggregationEvent. GS1 TDS 2.0 SGTIN-96 + SSCC-96 + GIAI-96 + GRAI-96 EPC schemes pre-encoded per programme.

features.title: Retailer programme readiness
features.text: Walmart Tier 2 + Tier 3 — apparel, footwear, home, hardlines, toys, jewelry, beauty. Target — apparel, accessories, home; SUPPLIERS portal compliance. Macy's, Nordstrom, Dick's, Lululemon — item-level RFID mandates. Decathlon — global apparel + sporting-goods RFID since 2014. ROI Audit + GS1 EPCIS event capture for Walmart Connect + Target + Sam's Club.

features.title: Reader hardware compatibility
features.text: Impinj Speedway R700 + R420 — 4-port fixed reader, 4 W EIRP; default for dock-door portal. Zebra FX9600 + FX7500 — fixed; FX7500 IP-65 rated for cold-DC. Impinj xSpan / xArray — overhead grid; retail floor + warehouse mezzanine. Handheld — Zebra RFD8500 (sub-zero spec), Impinj R1000, CipherLab RS35, Honeywell IH40. Reader middleware — Impinj ItemSense, Zebra ATR7000 / Savanna, NORDID, IDmicro, Pyramid Solutions Mosaic.

features.title: EPC pre-encoding service
features.text: Sequential — counter-up serial, customer-supplied GTIN-14 prefix. Random — non-sequential serial, customer-supplied prefix. Customer-supplied list — full EPC list provided as CSV; manifest-keyed to roll position. Lock bits + access password armed per programme spec. Per-roll EPC manifest in CSV or XML for downstream label-print correlation.

features.title: Procurement reality
features.text: MOQ 10,000 inlays / chip + antenna combo; 50,000 for fully-custom antenna design. Lead time 12-18 business days for stock chip / 4-6 weeks for fully-custom antenna. Unit price USD 0.04-0.18 ex-works depending on chip + antenna size + EPC pre-encoding + roll length. Per-roll quality pack — sensitivity histogram + yield report + EPC manifest + COA — included for orders ≥50,000.

features.title: What this inlay is NOT
features.text: Not a finished label — has no face stock, print, die-cut or top-coat. Not a HF NFC inlay — for tap-to-page consumer use, see nfc-dry-inlay / nfc-wet-inlay (NTAG21x). Not a UHF reader — pair with Impinj Speedway / Zebra FX9600 / handheld reader hardware. Not a temperature sensor — pair with Murata SL900A / Sensitech / ELPRO logger if cold-chain monitoring required.

faq.question: Which chip should I choose for retail apparel tagging?
faq.answer: For retail apparel, default to {chip:impinj-m730:name} (or its M750 high-encoding-speed variant) or {chip:nxp-ucode-8:name}. Both are the dominant 2024-2026 choices, both are Auburn ARC-W certified at default antenna sizes, both support GS1 SGTIN-96 EPC pre-encoding, and both are listed in the Walmart Tier 2/3, Target SUPPLIERS, Macy's, Nordstrom, Dick's, Lululemon and Decathlon vendor-compliance specifications. For premium / cold-DC programmes where 12-18 m read range matters, {chip:nxp-ucode-9:name} (best-in-class {chip:nxp-ucode-9:read_sensitivity_dbm} dBm sensitivity) is the upgrade. For reusable hard-tag retail security, {chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:name} remains the proven 5+ year workhorse. Send us your retailer mandate + Auburn ARC category and we match the chip + antenna combo + per-lot quality pack to that audit.

faq.question: What is the difference between wet and dry UHF inlays?
faq.answer: Wet inlays include a pressure-sensitive adhesive layer + silicone-coated PET release liner — they peel and stick directly onto a surface, or laminate into label stock at the converter (Mark Andy P5/P7, Nilpeter FA-17, MPS EF-Symjet). Dry inlays have no adhesive and no liner — they are designed for embedding into rigid housings (hard tags, ID-1 / CR-80 PVC cards, key fobs, RTI tags) via heat lamination, ultrasonic welding, ABS injection over-mold, or mechanical assembly. Same chip + antenna available in either format — choice is downstream-process driven. See the dedicated rfid-wet-inlay and rfid-dry-inlay SKUs for format-specific specs.

faq.question: Can you match a specific inlay used by our current supplier?
faq.answer: Yes. Send us a sample (3-5 pieces) or provide the inlay part number + roll spec sheet, and we identify the chip silicon ({chip:impinj-m730:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m770:short_name} / {chip:nxp-ucode-8:short_name} / 8m / 9 / {chip:impinj-monza-r6:short_name} / R6-P / {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name}), antenna geometry (dogbone / rectangular / short-dipole / near-field / square / web), pitch + chip position, web width and core size. We produce a compatible replacement inlay with equivalent or better Auburn ARC performance category. We maintain a library of industry-standard antenna designs compatible with major label converting platforms (Mark Andy, Nilpeter, MPS, Edale, Bobst, OMET) so equipment changeover is minimal.

faq.question: What pitch tolerance and web registration do converting lines running at 50-150 m/min require from inlay rolls?
faq.answer: Hold inlay pitch to ±0.5 mm and chip position to ±0.3 mm, or first-pass yield drops from ~99% to 80-90%. High-speed rotary label converting and print-and-apply lines (Mark Andy P5/P7, Nilpeter FA-17, MPS EF-Symjet, Edale FL3 at 50-150 m/min) need inlay pitch (centre-to-centre) held to ±0.5 mm and chip position within ±0.3 mm of nominal, otherwise encoder antenna coupling windows drift out of alignment and first-pass encoding yield collapses from ~99 % to 80-90 %. Our rolls are produced on flexo converting presses with servo-driven web registration and inline optical pitch verification; each roll ships with a measured pitch-distribution plot so converters can dial in their unwinder tension and encoder gantry position to the exact inlay geometry before production. Web widths: 50, 85, 110 mm; pitch options: 14, 18, 22, 25, 30, 35 mm or custom; core size 76.2 mm (3″).

faq.question: What incoming-quality documentation do retailer RFID programmes expect on every inlay lot?
faq.answer: Expect three artifacts per lot: a sensitivity histogram, a yield report and a GS1 SGTIN-96 EPC manifest. Programmes audited against Auburn University RFID Lab ARC categories and the retail RFID mandates (Walmart Tier 2/T3, Target SUPPLIERS, Macy's, Nordstrom, Dick's, Lululemon, Decathlon) increasingly require per-lot sensitivity histograms, yield reports and EPC pre-encoding manifests in CSV or XML aligned to the GS1 TDS 2.0 SGTIN-96 / SSCC-96 / GIAI-96 / GRAI-96 schemes. We provide all three with every shipment: the sensitivity histogram shows the dBm distribution across the 100 %-tested roll, the yield report states rejects-removed count + roll-position of removed inlays, and the EPC manifest is the full serialised list keyed to roll position so downstream label printers can correlate printed GTIN + serial to the encoded EPC for traceability. This documentation set is the dispute-resolution artifact at retailer receiving when DC-portal read rates fall below mandate thresholds.
